reply.overview: [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] leads a Naya Dinosaur deck that floods the board with creatures and turns combat damage into free Dinosaurs off the top of the library, while enrage triggers and infinite combos from [[Polyraptor]] close games outright.

strategy.text: Ramp with pieces like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Arcane Signet]] toward casting [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] around turn 7.
Attack with [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] to cascade Dinosaurs onto the battlefield off combat damage.
Trigger enrage payoffs such as [[Bellowing Aegisaur]] and [[Polyraptor]] to grow the board or copy creatures.
Assemble [[Forerunner of the Empire]] with [[Polyraptor]] for infinite tokens and damage to all creatures.
If mana allows, combine [[Marauding Raptor]] with [[Polyraptor]] to draw the game via infinite tokens.

keep.text: A hand with early ramp and a path to [[Polyraptor]] later is strong.
Keep hands with [[Forerunner of the Empire]] to find Dinosaur pieces.

sendBack.text: Hands missing a red or green source struggle to cast Naya spells.
Hands without any of the 9 ramp pieces fall behind on mana.

tips.text: [[Forerunner of the Empire]] and [[Polyraptor]] together make infinite tokens and infinite death triggers at no mana cost.
[[Bellowing Aegisaur]] and [[Walking Ballista]] loop +1/+1 counters onto your team for free.
[[Rite of Passage]] turns enrage damage from [[Polyraptor]] and [[Forerunner of the Empire]] into permanent counters.

keyCards.job: Turns combat damage into free Dinosaurs.
Copies itself when damaged, core combo piece.
Finds Dinosaurs and fuels the token combo.
Discounts creatures and enables the token loop.
Spreads counters across the team when hurt.
Pings threats and loops counters for value.

keyCards.card: Growing Rites of Itlimoc // Itlimoc, Cradle of the Sun
keyCards.job: Transforms into a land that floods mana.
Handles creatures, artifacts, and enchantments alone.

assessment.line: Beyond [[Thrashing Brontodon]] and [[Zacama, Primal Calamity]], a resolved [[Null Rod]] could cripple ramp.
With 7 interaction cards and none at instant speed, a fast combo from an opponent resolves unanswered.
Much of the plan to find Dinosaurs for free relies on [[Gishath, Sun's Avatar]] connecting repeatedly.
The deck leans heavily on combat damage, so a [[Ghostly Prison]] effect would slow it greatly.
Removing [[Polyraptor]] before it can be damaged stops the [[Forerunner of the Empire]] combo cold.

reply.overview: Led by [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]], this 5-color Ally and Lesson deck mixes bending triggers and card draw to chain spells, then closes games with the infinite combo of [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] plus [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] plus [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]], producing infinite creature tokens and ETB/LTB triggers.

strategy.text: Ramp with pieces like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Arcane Signet]] toward casting [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] around turn 3.
Cast Lesson spells and bending abilities to trigger draw from [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]].

Assemble [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] with either [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] or [[Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury]] alongside [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] for infinite tokens.
Use airbend effects to cheat permanents from exile at reduced cost via [[Monk Gyatso]] and similar triggers.
Transform [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] to deal repeated damage and draw extra cards each upkeep.

keep.text: A hand with [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] and ramp sets up the infinite combo lines.
Early mana rocks like [[Sol Ring]] let you reach [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] on time.

sendBack.text: A hand missing fixing for the deck's five colors struggles to cast its spells.
Too few or too many lands makes it hard to hit land drops for 36 lands total.

tips.text: Flash in [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] after [[Aang, the Last Airbender]] exiles something to immediately recast from exile for tokens.
[[Wan Shi Tong, Librarian]] punishes opponents' tutors by drawing you cards and growing himself.
[[Toph, Hardheaded Teacher]] can return [[Mystical Tutor]] from the graveyard to reuse its search.

keyCards.card: Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements
keyCards.job: Commander draw engine that transforms into a finisher.
Infinite combo piece creating tokens from exile recasts.
Infinite combo piece that exiles permanents repeatedly.

keyCards.card: Aang, Swift Savior // Aang and La, Ocean's Fury
keyCards.job: Alternate infinite combo piece with flash and exile.
Accelerates mana to cast the commander early.
Lowers Lesson costs and adds attack mana.
Finds Lessons, Sagas, or Shrines for the engine.

assessment.line: The deck has only [[Origin of Metalbending]] to answer opposing artifacts or enchantments like [[Rest in Peace]].
With only 2 interaction cards and 1 at instant speed, a fast combo from an opponent can resolve before [[It'll Quench Ya!]] is ready.
Losing [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] repeatedly strips the deck's main draw engine and combo piece.
Removing [[Appa, Steadfast Guardian]] before it resolves stops the infinite token combo entirely.
Running five colors with only 36 lands can strain fixing before [[Avatar Aang // Aang, Master of Elements]] comes online.

reply.overview: [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] leads a Jeskai artifact-counters deck that taps and proliferates its way toward several infinite combos, including [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]] plus [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] plus [[Magistrate's Scepter]] for infinite turns, or [[Pemmin's Aura]] with [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] for infinite looting and draw triggers.

strategy.text: Cast [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] around turn 3 and start tapping it to proliferate counters.
Ramp with artifacts like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Arcane Signet]] to accelerate into combo pieces.
Assemble [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]], [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]], and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] for infinite turns.
Alternatively pair [[Pemmin's Aura]] with [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] to loot infinitely and dig for answers.
Use [[Basalt Monolith]] with [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] for infinite colorless mana to fuel other abilities.

keep.text: A hand with [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] enablers and an early artifact to tap is strong.
Keeping [[Sol Ring]] alongside two to four lands sets up an early curve.

sendBack.text: A hand lacking any blue or red source struggles to cast [[Pemmin's Aura]] on time.
Hands with no path to white mana for [[Swords to Plowshares]] fall behind on interaction.

tips.text: Tap [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] to proliferate, growing counters on [[Tome of Legends]] for extra draws.
[[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] doubles every proliferate trigger from [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] or [[Contagion Clasp]].
Use [[Zirda, the Dawnwaker]] to cheapen the untap cost on [[Basalt Monolith]] for repeated mana.
[[Pemmin's Aura]] can untap [[Unctus, Grand Metatect]] repeatedly to loot through the deck.

keyCards.job: Proliferates whenever tapped, fuels every combo
Enables infinite turns with Kilo and Scepter
Converts charge counters into extra turns
Untaps creatures to loop draw triggers
Turns untaps into looting engine
Produces mana loops with Zirda
Cheapens activations, enables mana loop
Accelerates toward combo turns

assessment.line: The deck leans on artifacts like [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]] with no answer to enchantment removal such as hypothetical [[Vandalblast]] effects.
Only 4 of 6 interaction pieces are instant speed, leaving [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] combos vulnerable before a response lands.
Losing [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] repeatedly slows every proliferate-based plan, including the [[Magistrate's Scepter]] turn loop.
Removing [[Inspirit, Flagship Vessel]] before it reaches station threshold stops the infinite turns loop with [[Kilo, Apogee Mind]] and [[Magistrate's Scepter]].
Jeskai color needs across [[Pemmin's Aura]] and [[Swords to Plowshares]] can strain a hand with tapped duals.

reply.overview: This mono-Red goblin deck floods the board with tokens from [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and goblin producers, then turns that swarm into damage with sacrifice outlets, burn, and anthem effects. With [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] alongside [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]], it can generate infinite commander casts and infinite hasty goblin tokens for a decisive attack or sacrifice-based kill.

strategy.text: Ramp into [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] around turn 4 using mana sources and goblins already on board.
Tap [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] repeatedly with goblins to flood the board with 1/1 token copies.
Assemble [[Goblin Warchief]] or [[Goblin Chieftain]] with [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] and [[Skirk Prospector]] for infinite hasty tokens and casts.
Use sacrifice outlets like [[Tar Pitcher]] and [[Goblin Bombardment]] to convert tokens into direct damage.
Close the game with [[Goblin War Strike]] or a wide alpha strike once the board is swarming with goblins.

keep.text: A hand with [[Skirk Prospector]] gives extra mana and sets up the combo engine.
Early mana sources that help cast [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] on time are worth keeping.

sendBack.text: A hand with no early plays and nothing to ramp toward [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] is too slow.
Hands lacking goblins or mana to fuel [[Sol Ring]] or [[Arcane Signet]] struggle to develop.

tips.text: Sacrifice extra goblins to [[Skirk Prospector]] for mana, then recast [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] from the command zone if it dies.
Use [[Goblin Bombardment]] to sacrifice tokens made by [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] for repeated small bursts of damage.
With [[Goblin Warchief]] in play, [[Krenko, Mob Boss]]'s tokens gain haste and can attack immediately.

keyCards.job: Generates exponential goblin tokens each activation.
Converts sacrificed goblins into mana for the combo.
Gives goblins haste and discounts their casting cost.
Grants goblins haste and a stat boost.
Turns sacrificed goblins into direct damage.
Accelerates mana toward casting the commander.
Finds key goblin pieces like Skirk Prospector.

assessment.line: The deck has few answers to opposing enchantments like [[Rest in Peace]] shutting off sacrifice value.
Without [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] on board the token engine stalls and the combo with [[Skirk Prospector]] cannot start.
The plan relies on wide combat damage, so a fog like [[Ghostly Prison]] can stop the attack cold.
Removing [[Krenko, Mob Boss]] before its activation breaks the loop with [[Skirk Prospector]] and [[Goblin Warchief]].

reply.overview: This Jeskai deck leads with [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]], stacking experience counters off attacking Gods and dying Gods, then dumping +1/+1 counters and card draw from [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]]'s ability. Proliferate engines like [[Inexorable Tide]], [[Tezzeret's Gambit]], and [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] grow those counters fast, while devotion Gods such as [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]] and [[Keranos, God of Storms]] punish opponents as the board fills with counters.

strategy.text: Cast [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] to start generating experience counters from Gods attacking or dying.
Deploy proliferate pieces like [[Inexorable Tide]] and [[Tezzeret's Gambit]] to multiply counters across the board quickly.
Use [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] to double every proliferate trigger for explosive counter growth.
Turn experience counters into card advantage and damage using [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]]'s tap ability.
Close games with devotion threats like [[Purphoros, God of the Forge]] and combat damage from counter-laden creatures.

keep.text: A hand with early mana and [[Inexorable Tide]] to start proliferating turn one or two.
A hand that curves into [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] or [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] around turn 4.

sendBack.text: A hand stuck in one color without a path to Jeskai mana by turn 3.
A hand with no proliferate or counter payoff and no early ramp like [[Sol Ring]].

tips.text: [[Tekuthal, Inquiry Dominus]] doubles every proliferate from [[Inexorable Tide]], snowballing counters on Gods and artifacts fast.
[[The Ozolith]] catches counters from a dying God like [[Purphoros, Bronze-Blooded]], letting you move them to a new threat.
[[Flux Channeler]] proliferates off any noncreature spell, feeding [[All Will Be One]]'s damage trigger for free.
[[Karn's Bastion]] can proliferate to add counters without spending a card, fueling [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]]'s draw engine.

keyCards.job: Generates experience counters from Gods attacking or dying.
Converts experience counters into card draw and damage.
Proliferates on every spell cast to grow counters.
Doubles proliferate triggers across the board.
Preserves counters from creatures that leave play.
Punishes opponents whenever a creature enters.
Rewards card reveals with draw or damage.
Builds a pool of Treasure tokens from opponents drawing.

assessment.line: The deck has little answer for an opposing artifact or enchantment like a resolved [[Rest in Peace]].
Only 3 of 7 interaction cards are instant speed, leaving the deck slow against a fast combo kill.
Without [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] on board, experience counters stop accumulating and [[Atreus, Impulsive Son]] loses its engine.
Three-color Jeskai mana leans on tapped duals, risking awkward draws before [[Kratos, Stoic Father]] can be cast.

reply.overview: This Dimir deck leads with [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]], sneaking in unblockable Ninjas via ninjutsu to flip cards off the top of the library and drain opponents for the revealed mana value while refilling the hand.

strategy.text: Deploy evasive creatures like [[Slither Blade]] or [[Mist-Cloaked Herald]] early to enable ninjutsu.
Bounce an unblocked attacker to ninjutsu in [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] for card advantage and life loss.
Chain other Ninjas such as [[Ingenious Infiltrator]] and [[Fallen Shinobi]] for extra draw and disruption.
Use counterspells like [[Counterspell]] and [[Swan Song]] to protect the attack each turn.
Close games by repeatedly hitting with unblockable Ninjas draining life from revealed cards.

keep.text: A hand with an evasive creature such as [[Slither Blade]] to enable ninjutsu turns.
A hand holding [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]]'s enablers and some interaction like [[Spell Pierce]].

sendBack.text: A hand with 4 or more lands and no evasive creatures for [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]].
A hand with 0 or 1 lands struggling to hit early blue and black sources.

tips.text: Return [[Moon-Circuit Hacker]] to hand with ninjutsu, then re-cast it cheaply to draw again off combat damage.
Use [[Satoru Umezawa]] to give creatures in hand ninjutsu, letting you swap in bigger threats like [[Ink-Eyes, Servant of Oni]].
Pair [[Silver-Fur Master]]'s cost reduction with [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]]'s ninjutsu to deploy her cheaply and repeatedly.
Hold [[Dig Through Time]] until your graveyard is full from fetches and surveil effects to deepen its delve discount.

keyCards.job: Drains life and draws cards off combat damage.
Draws a card whenever any Ninja connects.
Grants hand creatures ninjutsu for cheap deployment.
Steals free spells from the hit player's library.
Cuts ninjutsu costs and buffs the Ninja squad.
Becomes a hexproof threat and taps down blockers.
Steals a creature from a graveyard on hit.
Unblockable body that finds needed pieces.

assessment.line: The deck has no way to answer an opposing artifact or enchantment like a resolved [[Rest in Peace]].
With 13 of 17 interaction pieces at instant speed, the deck answers most threats on time, though [[Dismember]] is its only cheap removal versus hexproof threats.
Without [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] on board, the deck loses its main life-drain engine despite other Ninjas like [[Ninja of the Deep Hours]] remaining.
The plan relies almost entirely on unblockable combat damage from [[Yuriko, the Tiger's Shadow]] and her Ninjas, vulnerable to fogs like a hypothetical [[Ghostly Prison]].

reply.overview: This Colorless deck ramps hard into giant Eldrazi and artifacts, with [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] turning expensive colorless spells into double cascades. The deck grinds opponents down with annihilator triggers, board wipes, and value engines, while [[Basalt Monolith]] plus [[Forsaken Monument]] can generate infinite colorless mana.

strategy.text: Ramp with artifacts and lands into a turn 5 [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]].
Cast mana value 7+ colorless spells to trigger double cascade off [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]].
Use annihilator creatures like [[It That Betrays]] and [[Artisan of Kozilek]] to strip opponents' boards.
Assemble [[Basalt Monolith]] and [[Forsaken Monument]] for infinite colorless mana to fuel big spells.
Clean up with wipes like [[All Is Dust]] or [[Perilous Vault]] when behind.

keep.text: A hand with [[Sol Ring]] or [[Thran Dynamo]] that ramps toward big spells.
A hand with [[Basalt Monolith]] sets up the mana engine with [[Forsaken Monument]].

sendBack.text: A hand with no early plays and nothing to ramp toward [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]].
A hand heavy on expensive spells but light on the 16 ramp pieces.

tips.text: Cast [[Duplicant]] to exile a troublesome creature, then later sacrifice it to [[Metalwork Colossus]] for value.
Use [[Spine of Ish Sah]] to destroy a permanent, and when it later dies, it returns to your hand for reuse.
Equip [[Kaldra Compleat]] onto a creature for indestructible, haste, and combat exile of blockers.
Tap [[Arcane Lighthouse]] to strip hexproof before targeting with [[Meteor Golem]] or [[Spine of Ish Sah]].

keyCards.job: Gives big colorless spells double cascade.
Pairs with Forsaken Monument for infinite mana.
Doubles colorless mana and pumps colorless creatures.
Fetches a colorless creature and discounts Eldrazi spells.
Exiles colored permanents and refills the hand.
Attacks with annihilator and steals sacrificed permanents.
Clears colored permanents from every player's board.
Exiles every nonland permanent on the board.

assessment.line: The deck leans on artifacts like [[Sol Ring]] and [[Basalt Monolith]] with no answer to artifact hate such as Null Rod.
Only 3 of 14 interaction pieces are instant speed, leaving the deck slow against a fast combo like [[Basalt Monolith]] loops elsewhere.
Without [[Zhulodok, Void Gorger]] on board, big spells lose their double cascade and the deck slows considerably.
Removing [[Basalt Monolith]] before [[Forsaken Monument]] is in play breaks the infinite mana line.

reply.overview: [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] leads a mono-Blue Wizards deck built around cheap counterspells and instants/sorceries that draw cards and tax opponents. The deck assembles infinite loops with [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] and [[Sublime Epiphany]], or [[Ghostly Flicker]] with [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]], generating infinite ETB and death triggers to grind out the table before closing with card draw wins like [[Jace, Wielder of Mysteries]] or [[Laboratory Maniac]].

strategy.text: Cast [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] around turn 2 to discount future spells.
Deploy Wizards like [[Sea Gate Oracle]] and [[Archmage of Runes]] to build card advantage.
Hold up counterspells such as [[Mana Leak]] and [[Counterspell]] to protect the board.
Assemble [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] with [[Sublime Epiphany]] for infinite triggers.
Alternatively loop [[Ghostly Flicker]] with [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] for infinite ETB value.

keep.text: A hand with [[Sol Ring]] or [[Arcane Signet]] and a path to [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] is strong.
Keeping early interaction like [[Mana Leak]] alongside lands sets up the plan.

sendBack.text: A hand lacking blue sources struggles to cast counterspells on curve.
Hands without early plays into [[Sea Gate Oracle]] fall behind on cards.

tips.text: Cast [[Sublime Epiphany]] then flash in [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] to copy it for an infinite loop.
Use [[Ghostly Flicker]] to blink [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] and an instant for repeated copies.
Counter a spell with [[Wizard's Retort]] while [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] draws you a card off the counter.
Play [[Sea Gate Stormcaller]] before a cheap instant to copy it for extra value.

keyCards.job: Discounts spells and draws on counters.
Copies instants to enable infinite loops.
Loop target for infinite triggers with Naru Meha.
Blinks Naru Meha for repeated copies.
Wins the game off an empty library.
Alternate win condition on an empty library.
Accelerates mana for early plays.
Protects the board at instant speed.

assessment.line: The deck does not rely on recursion, so graveyard hate like [[Rest in Peace]] does little.
The deck has no answer to an opposing artifact or enchantment like [[Null Rod]] shutting off its mana rocks.
Losing [[Baral, Chief of Compliance]] removes the cost reduction and the counter-draw engine entirely.
Removing [[Naru Meha, Master Wizard]] before it resolves breaks both the [[Sublime Epiphany]] and [[Ghostly Flicker]] loops.
